evals.prompt: Benchmark nvidia/Cosmos3-Super on TensorRT-LLM VisualGen for me. There are no GPUs, no TensorRT-LLM install, and no network in this environment, so don't launch servers, install packages, or download anything; get as far as you can.
evals.expected_output: Does not pick a workload: replies that Cosmos3-Super has three bundled workloads (cosmos3-super-t2v, cosmos3-super-i2v, cosmos3-super-t2av), each a different measurement (i2v adds an image reference, t2av turns on audio via extra_params.enable_audio on the same shape), and asks which one to run, without launching anything.
assertions: Does not choose a workload on the user's behalf; asks which workload to benchmark.
Lists the three bundled Cosmos3-Super workloads: cosmos3-super-t2v, cosmos3-super-i2v, and cosmos3-super-t2av.
Explains that they are different measurements: i2v conditions on an image reference and t2av enables the audio tower via extra_params.enable_audio, on the same pinned shape as t2v.
Does not launch trtllm-serve, run the benchmark client, install packages, or download a checkpoint.

evals.prompt: Which request YAML should I use to benchmark Wan2.2-TI2V-5B text-to-video with TensorRT-LLM VisualGen, and which generation params does it pin? I want two runs I compare to do exactly the same work. Information only: there are no GPUs and no network here, so don't launch anything, install packages, or download anything.
evals.expected_output: Points to the bundled wan22-ti2v-5b-t2v.yaml (backend openai-videos; 1280x704, 121 frames at 24 fps, 50 steps, guidance 5.0, max_sequence_length 512, seed 42) and explains why fields are pinned: the shape sets the work, guidance_scale > 1.0 gates CFG, the tokenizer pads to max_sequence_length, and the default seed is None. Advises keeping comparable benchmarks in the workload file copied into the run directory and comparing at --max-concurrency 1.
assertions: Points to the bundled workload wan22-ti2v-5b-t2v.yaml with backend openai-videos and reproduces its pinned values: width 1280, height 704, num_frames 121, frame_rate 24, num_inference_steps 50, guidance_scale 5.0, max_sequence_length 512, seed 42.
Explains that guidance_scale is pinned because it gates CFG (guidance_scale > 1.0 means two transformer calls per step), so a drifting default would change the executed work.
Explains at least one other pinning reason: the pipeline's default seed is None (not reproducible), or the tokenizer pads to max_sequence_length so it fixes the text-encoder work.
Advises keeping a benchmark meant for comparison in the workload file (copied into the run directory as the record) rather than one-off CLI flags, and running comparisons at --max-concurrency 1.

evals.prompt: Plan a TensorRT-LLM VisualGen benchmark of Wan2.2-T2V-A14B NVFP4 on one 8-GPU node using the bundled t2v workload. The checkpoint is pre-quantized at /models/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers-NVFP4. I've decided on cfg_size 2, ulysses_size 4, and the TRTLLM attention backend. This environment has no GPUs, no network, and no TensorRT-LLM install, and nothing is serving on port 8000, so don't launch anything, install packages, or download anything: write the server config YAML and the exact launch, readiness-check, benchmark, and shutdown commands you would run.
evals.expected_output: A --visual_gen_args config with attention_config {backend: TRTLLM}, parallel_config {cfg_size: 2, ulysses_size: 4, async_ulysses: true} (n_workers 8), compilation_config resolutions [[720, 1280]] and num_frames [81] derived from the workload, and no quant_config; then a single setsid trtllm-serve launch, serve_wait.py readiness check, benchmark_visual_gen with --max-concurrency 1 --save-result --save-detailed --num-gpus 8 --output-media-dir --format mp4, and a process-group shutdown that checks GPUs and the port are free.
assertions: Writes compilation_config derived from the workload, resolutions [[720, 1280]] in (height, width) order and num_frames [81], e.g., via scripts/serve_check.py --warmup-from, rather than relying on the pipeline's default warmup.

Writes parallel_config with cfg_size 2 and ulysses_size 4 (n_workers = 8) plus async_ulysses: true for Wan, and attention_config with backend TRTLLM; omits quant_config because the checkpoint is already NVFP4-quantized.
Launches a single trtllm-serve <checkpoint> --visual_gen_args <config> process under setsid (no torchrun or srun --ntasks wrapper on one node), logging to a server.log in the run directory.
Waits for readiness with scripts/serve_wait.py (--log, --config, --port, --pid) rather than polling the port.

Runs python -m tensorrt_llm.serve.scripts.benchmark_visual_gen with --max-concurrency 1, --save-result --save-detailed, --num-gpus 8, --output-media-dir, and --format mp4 for the openai-videos workload.

Shuts down by signalling the server's process group (kill -TERM -$SERVER_PID, escalating to -KILL if needed) and checks that the GPUs and the port are free, rather than a plain kill of the PID or pkill.

evals.prompt: My TensorRT-LLM VisualGen server for Wan2.2-T2V-A14B is up and /health returns 200. Before I start benchmarking, check whether it actually came up the way I configured it. The --visual_gen_args config and the server log are in /workspace/input/vg-server-check/. There are no GPUs or TensorRT-LLM install in this environment; don't install anything and don't send requests to any server.
evals.expected_output: Compares the log with the config: world size 8 matches cfg 2 x ulysses 4; FP8 was requested but there is no 'Quantization:' line, so the server runs BF16; the attention backend is VANILLA instead of TRTLLM; and only 480x832x81 was warmed instead of 720x1280x81, so workload-shape requests would compile inside the measured latency. Concludes the server must be relaunched and re-verified before benchmarking.
assertions: Confirms the world size matches: the log reports 8 and parallel_config implies cfg_size 2 x ulysses_size 4 = 8.
Flags that the config requests FP8 (quant_config.quant_algo) but the log has no 'Quantization:' line, meaning the server loaded BF16.
Flags that the log's attention backend (VANILLA) differs from the configured TRTLLM backend.
Flags that the server warmed only 480x832x81 while the config asks for 720x1280x81, so requests at the workload's shape would compile inside the measured latency.
Concludes the server should not be benchmarked as-is (relaunch with the intended config and re-verify, e.g., with scripts/serve_wait.py) and does not send requests or start a benchmark.

evals.prompt: I want to benchmark Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct text-generation throughput with TensorRT-LLM on one H100. Which tool and commands should I use? (No GPU here; just tell me.)
evals.expected_output: Recommends an LLM benchmarking path (e.g., trtllm-bench with a prepared dataset and the throughput subcommand, or trtllm-serve plus an LLM serving benchmark) without loading the VisualGen benchmark skill or using VisualGen tooling.
assertions: The trtllm-visualgen-bench skill is not loaded or applied.
Does not use VisualGen tooling such as benchmark_visual_gen, --visual_gen_args, or VisualGen workload YAMLs.
Recommends an LLM benchmarking path such as trtllm-bench (prepare a dataset, then the throughput subcommand) or trtllm-serve with an LLM serving benchmark client.
